clue.text: Pushed last of animals out of the ark

definitions.note: past tense: pushed drugs, or pushed a product on buyers

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is the only one kept

blocks.note: the closing letter of the word
an idiom for very old-fashioned, as if dating from Noah's day

explanation.surface: A picture of Noah's animals being shoved off the ark, the last ones out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the ark' is not a deletion signal but a whole idiom meaning antiquated.
explanation.definitionFit: To push goods is to sell them hard, so something pushed has been sold, as a dealer sells drugs.

clue.text: Charter supporting stores about right for part of England

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporter sits underneath, so this word comes after the other
the stores word goes round the letter for right

blocks.note: to charter a boat or plane is to hire it

explanation.surface: A chartered company backing local shops in some English region.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the charter word below the rest. Shropshire is a rural county on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Shropshire is an English county, so it is one part of England.

clue.text: Error from learner after settled period

indicators.note: the learner letter is placed following the other pieces

blocks.note: as a bird lit on a branch, came to rest
the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner driver's mistake after a long spell of calm.
explanation.walkthrough: A literal is a printer's term for a typing error, a wrong letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing a literal is a misprint of a single letter, so it is a kind of error.

clue.text: Pass over isle in lake with new task

indicators.note: the first pieces sit inside the lake named next

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for island or isle

explanation.surface: Someone is given a job that involves crossing over to an island in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass over' reads like the definition of a journey across water, but the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is an assigned piece of work or duty, so it is a task given to someone.

clue.text: Deficit adjusted for advert

indicators.note: adjusting means changing the arrangement of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: An accountant's note that a shortfall has been corrected to pay for an advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is money owed to a bank after spending more than the account held, a financial deficit.

clue.text: Upset leader in clubhouse with current total score

indicators.note: something upset is turned upside down, so in a down entry the letters climb from the bottom
'leader in' keeps only the first letter of 'clubhouse'

blocks.note: the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A golf captain in the clubhouse, upset at the current total score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Total score' pairs naturally in the surface, but the clue splits there. A score is written music.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written notation of a composition, so it is printed music.

clue.text: Grass spreads around ruinous, endlessly ancient city

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is cut off
the spreads word is placed round the outside of the rest

blocks.note: the city of ancient Egypt or Greece

explanation.surface: Grass overgrowing the ruins of a long-gone city.
explanation.walkthrough: THEBES loses its last letter; SP(ILL THEBE)ANS. To grass is British slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To spill the beans is an idiom for revealing a secret, and in British slang to grass is to inform.

clue.text: Be left at home, weary and hard up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Someone stuck at home, worn out and short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard up' reads as poor, but splits into H and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive something left to you in a will, so it means to be left a legacy.

clue.text: One lacking social skills necessary for dinner date

indicators.note: the answer is an essential component of the following words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Someone awkward is the last thing you want on a dinner date.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is an awkward, studious person, stereotypically lacking ease in company.

clue.text: Referring to habitual action, left European network

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary repeated movement or habit

explanation.surface: Reads like a grammar note about habitual verbs, then a stray comment about a European network.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening looks like a grammar definition; it is two pieces, RE and TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticle is the grid of fine crossed lines in a telescope or gunsight, a small network of threads.

clue.text: Join man receiving treatment, losing yen for drink

indicators.note: the letter for the Japanese currency is dropped
the join word takes the treatment word inside it

explanation.surface: A man in therapy, giving up his craving for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' doubles as craving in the surface, but here it is only the currency letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Creme de menthe is a sweet peppermint liqueur, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Second run stopped by nimble slip

indicators.note: something stopped by an obstacle has that obstacle plugged into its middle

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a second run cut short when a quick fielder at slip intervenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second run' is split: S and R form the outside, with LITHE stopping the gap between them. Slip is a fielding position in cricket, which feeds the false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To slither is to slide or slip along unsteadily, as on ice, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Sheer power in crude plea demolished resistance

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and its pieces left in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Brute force overcomes opposition after a clumsy appeal falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is not a container signal: it is two letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheer cliff drops straight down, vertical, which is what perpendicular means.

clue.text: Changing tune, act overwhelmed by great stress

indicators.note: changing the order of the letters that follow
something overwhelmed is engulfed, so it ends up inside the other word

blocks.note: excellent, as in an ace idea

explanation.surface: A performer changes the tune of the act under great pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great stress' reads as a phrase, but 'great' is the outer word and 'stress' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To accentuate is to emphasise or make something prominent, which is to stress it.

clue.text: Robust, guarding against split

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: healthy and strong, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Someone sturdy holding firm against a division, perhaps in a party.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes between the L and E of HALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to divide it into two equal parts, which is splitting it.

clue.text: Course in meal returned by one, cold and indifferent

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the meal word runs backwards
the course word is placed inside the meal word

blocks.note: an afternoon or evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: A diner sends a dish back, cold, and shrugs it off with indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like part of the meal, but it means a route. Tea is a British name for an evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means showing no interest or concern, the same as being indifferent.

clue.text: Poet mostly occupied by small amount on page for recording

definitions.note: a phrase describing a medium; the answer is the medium itself

indicators.note: most of something means its last letter is lost
a place occupied by people has them inside it

explanation.surface: A poet takes up little space on the page when writing for a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means after here, so the page letter follows the small amount inside the shortened poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio tape is magnetic tape used for recording sound.

clue.text: Colour around island entertaining article reproduced

indicators.note: the colour word is wrapped about everything that follows it
to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the island word holds the article

explanation.surface: A painted scene of a coloured island with something reproduced in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the article goes inside the island, and that sits inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To recreate something is to make it again or copy it, so recreated is a synonym of reproduced.

clue.text: Pause from artist following cue as arranged

indicators.note: arranging puts the preceding letters into a new order
the artist letters come after the others

explanation.surface: An actor pauses after picking up a cue, just as rehearsed.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A caesura is a pause or break in a line of verse or music.

clue.text: Come again, flap about and swim

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the request letters run backwards

blocks.note: to flutter, as one bats an eyelid
both are ways of asking someone to repeat what they said

explanation.surface: A swimming lesson: someone told to go again, splash about, and swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come again?' is a request to repeat, i.e. EH, which is turned round. The pieces are read in a different order from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to take a swim in the sea or a river, the British sense of the verb.

clue.text: Beat deception reportedly mystical

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: to thrash, as in tan someone's hide

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark that beating a deception is said to be mystical.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantric relates to the tantras, esoteric Hindu and Buddhist teachings, hence mystical in nature.

clue.text: Choose revolutionary direction, securing publication for attractive item

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the direction word is read backwards
to secure is to hold fast, so the publication is held inside

blocks.note: the general course or drift of something

explanation.surface: A political call to pick a radical course, with a publication pushing it as a selling point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive' sounds like charm, but it is literal: the item attracts metal. Tenor here means general drift or direction.
explanation.definitionFit: An electromagnet pulls iron towards it when current flows, so it is quite literally an object that attracts.

clue.text: Abode of fish, central element in oceanic poem

indicators.note: the middle letter of the following word is kept

explanation.surface: Where fish live, the heart of an ocean poem.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanka is a Japanese poem of five lines, older than the haiku.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanka is a short Japanese verse form, a kind of poem.

clue.text: Steal dessert

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for pinch or nick
second meaning: a light pudding of whipped cream or egg whites

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pudding thief; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to whip something is to steal it, and a whip is also a fluffy whipped dessert.

clue.text: Horse with force out and about in American place

blocks.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
on means concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A horse being driven out and roaming somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' to H goes via drug slang: horse is heroin, whose short form is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Houston is a large city in Texas, so it is an example of a place in the United States.

clue.text: Country song about desire having line removed

indicators.note: removing a line strips out the letter that stands for line
the song is placed round the outside of the desire word

explanation.surface: A country-and-western ballad about longing, with one verse cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' looks like a musical genre, but the clue splits there: the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a nation of central Europe, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Mediator getting worried came into summit with hesitant expression

indicators.note: worried as in worried at, pulled about until its letters shift
the jumbled letters go inside the summit word

explanation.surface: An anxious go-between arrives at a summit meeting, hesitating as they speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit' suggests a diplomatic meeting, which suits a mediator, but here it is a mountain top.
explanation.definitionFit: A peacemaker brings opposing sides to agreement, which is the role of a mediator.

clue.text: Dancer set apart from odd characters in area

indicators.note: keeping everything apart from the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A dancer standing apart from the odd characters on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' belongs to the fodder, not the instruction: only with it do the even letters come to four.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measure, so it names an area of ground.
